title: The other you
summary: A photo of you signing a baby's babygro at a christening you never went to. The man in it is Lee, he washes cars by the ring road, and he has your face. A season on you're in goal at his Sunday side's penalty night, and then your mum sees his picture in the paper and goes very quiet.

ends.title: Sunday dinner
ends.text: Lee comes for Sunday dinner now. Your mum does his plate first and nobody says why.

ends.title: The other you
ends.text: Lee does openings and christenings as you, forty quid a time. He sends you a card every Christmas signed with your name.

ends.title: Never met again
ends.text: You never saw Lee again. Now and then somebody tells you they met you at a wedding, and you say thanks.

beats.title: The christening

event.title: The christening
event.speaker: pal
setup: {pal.short} sends a photo at eleven at night. It's you, in a grey suit, holding a baby in a church in a town you've never been to, signing the babygro with a felt tip.
"Didn't know you did christenings. Cousin's mate's lad. They're made up."

say: "It's you, isn't it? Tell me it's you."
You zoom in. Same nose. Same ears. He's even got the bit of hair that won't lie down.

replies.label: "It isn't. Find out who he is."
"I'm sending it to the club's lawyers."

say: Ten minutes later. "His name's Lee. Works at the hand car wash on the ring road. My cousin says he's been doing it for a free pint."

replies.label: "A free pint. Leave him to it."

go.text: {pal.short} sends the address and a row of crying-laughing faces. You tell him you'll go Saturday after the game.

leave.text: You put the phone face down. Then you pick it up and look again.

lawyers.text: The club's solicitor writes to a car wash. Nobody writes back.

beats.hint: Your mate has a photo of you at a christening you never went to

beats.title: The car wash

event.title: The car wash
event.speaker: pal
setup: The hand car wash behind the tyre place. A lad in a wet tracksuit is doing the wheels on a van, and when he stands up it's like a mirror that's had a hard week.
{if arc.path=='lawyers'}He's got the solicitor's letter in his back pocket. It's gone soft in the rain.{/if}

say: "Lee," he says, and wipes his hand on his leg before he holds it out. "I know. I KNOW. I never said I was you. I just never said I wasn't."

replies.label: "Do you want one signed by the real one?"
"Fancy doing a sponsor shoot for me on Tuesday?"

mate.text: You sign his tracksuit top and he does your car for nothing. He does it badly. You both laugh at the same moment, the same laugh.

stop.text: He goes red and says sorry about four times. On the way out you see him in your wing mirror, watching you go.

use.text: He does two hours under the lights in a boot advert, and the photographer never knows. The sponsor says it's your best shoot yet.

beats.hint: Lee works at the car wash on the ring road

beats.title: His Sunday side

event.title: His Sunday side
event.speaker: pal
setup: A season on. Lee's Sunday side, the Crown and Anchor, are raising money for a minibus. A pound a penalty, and the whole pub wants to see the two of you on one pitch.
{if arc.mid=='stop'}He's stopped doing christenings. He says the pub won't let him forget it.{/if}{if arc.mid=='use'}He's got his own agent now. It's his brother-in-law.{/if}

say: {pal.short} has driven you down. "Ten balls, him behind you calling the corners like he's your dad. Half the pub thinks you're both him."

replies.label: "Not tonight. Put me down for fifty quid."

say: The park, two floodlights on a generator, forty people with pints in plastic glasses.

rounds.line: Lee shouts the corner. Same voice as yours.

lines.hit: "That's him. Or that's the other one."

say: You stop there and hand the ball back.
{activity.score} out of ten. Not bad at all.

good.text: The pub raises four hundred and twelve pounds. Lee buys the minibus a sticker with both your faces on it.

poor.text: You miss more than you score and the pub chants Lee's name. He takes a bow you've seen yourself do on the telly.

stop.text: You hand {pal.short} the ball and say you've a game Saturday. Lee takes the rest in your place, and the pub can't tell.

paid.text: You send fifty quid. The Crown and Anchor's minibus has a sticker on the back: SPONSORED BY BOTH OF THEM.

beats.hint: A season on: Lee's Sunday side want you for their penalty night

beats.title: The paper

event.title: The paper
event.speaker: pal
setup: Sunday's {tabloid.outlet}: "STAR'S SECRET TWIN?" Two photos side by side, you at the ground and Lee with a sponge. {tabloid.name} wants a quote by six.
Your mum rings, and she doesn't say hello. "What's his birthday?"

say: "Same as yours, isn't it." She isn't asking. "The General. There was a girl in the next bed, sixteen, on her own. Nine pound two, her boy was. Same as you. I always wondered."

replies.label: "Shall I ask him round on Sunday?"

say: A long breath down the phone. "And what would we do with it, love?"

test.text: You both spit in a tube that the tabloid paid for. You're not related. Lee rings to say he's gutted, and he sounds it.

dinner.text: Lee comes round in a borrowed shirt with a cake from the garage. Your mum keeps putting her hand on his arm.

leave.text: You give the paper nothing. Your mum doesn't bring it up again, and you can hear her not bringing it up.

beats.hint: Your mum has seen Lee in the paper

event.title: Lee
event.speaker: pal
setup: Years on. A man in the front row of the family stand has your face, a bit heavier now, and a lad on his shoulders in your shirt.
{if arc.mum=='dinner'}Your mum's beside them with a flask.{/if}

say: {pal.short} spots him first. "Is that Lee? Go on. Go over."

replies.label: Go over to the front row.

over.text: You sign the lad's shirt and Lee says, "Tell him who's the better looking one." The lad says you.
He takes a selfie of the three of you. By teatime it's on the car wash's page with a price list.

wave.text: He waves back with both arms. Somebody near him says it's you, waving at yourself.
He waves back, then picks his lad up so he can see you.

tunnel.text: When you look back from the tunnel he's gone, or he's somebody else.
